task_text: Fix split_fields(text) in solution.py. Unescaped commas split fields; backslash escapes ONLY comma or backslash; preserve empty fields including trailing ones. Empty input returns ['']. Invalid escape or dangling backslash raises ValueError. No imports or external dependencies. Return full solution.py in files, with only pure functions; allowed built-ins len/range/enumerate/zip/sorted/list/tuple/str/int/float/bool/abs/min/max/sum/round/ValueError; the only allowed method call is list.append. Do not include grading tests. answer may briefly identify the implementation. Host checks run separately. Inputs are strings, at most80 characters.

answer.approach: single-pass state machine over characters with an 'escaped' flag

response.concise_method_summary: split_fields scans the input one character at a time keeping an 'escaped' boolean. Outside escape state, a comma closes the current field (appended to the result list, buffer reset) and any other character (including backslash, which flips 'escaped' on) is otherwise accumulated. While 'escaped' is set, only ',' or '\\' are valid and are appended literally to the current field before the flag is cleared; any other character raises ValueError for an invalid escape. After the scan, a still-set 'escaped' flag means a dangling trailing backslash, which also raises ValueError. The final (possibly empty) buffer is always appended, which naturally yields [''] for empty input and preserves empty leading/trailing/interior fields since every comma boundary is recorded regardless of buffer content. Only list.append is used as a method call; string building uses '+' and comparisons, satisfying the restricted built-in/method surface.
assumptions: Backslash is only a meta-character when immediately followed by ',' or '\\'; any other char after '\\' is an invalid escape.
A field-separating comma must itself be unescaped; an escaped comma ('\\,') is treated as a literal comma in the field content.
Empty string input returns [''] per spec; this falls out of the general scan since the trailing buffer is always appended.
Input length is bounded (<=80 chars) so no performance concerns from the linear single pass.
No other escape sequences (e.g. \n, \t) are meaningful; only comma and backslash are legal escape targets.
